source:
tao says a window has left full screen as soon as it is asked to, so a
hide landed mid-exit and the exit's end put the window back; 583bc3b74
kept hiding it every 200 ms for up to 5 s. Now a close in full screen
watches the main window's NSWindowDidExitFullScreenNotification (from the
first such close on, through juggler-window-events' audit 8), sets the
hide to wait on it, leaves full screen, and hides once when the event
comes; resizes on the way out do nothing. Only if no event comes within
5 s does the fallback (583bc3b74's looks) take over, and it alone runs
when the event can't be watched. A show calls either off.

The decisions are HideAfterExit (close, exited, call_off, fall_back,
resized, settle) and event_or_fallback, over the Hide trait. Logged:
'leaving it first; it hides on the exit event' or '... by the fallback',
then 'hidden on the exit event', or 'no exit event within 5 s; the
fallback hides the window' and 'done by the fallback'; 'called off, the
window was shown again'; 'the exit event can't be watched (…)'.

Tests: the event hides the window once and no fallback follows (a resize
mid-exit, a second event and a late look hide nothing); no event in 5 s
and the fallback hides it, a late event doing nothing; a show before the
